title: Review: Forces and free-body diagrams; Newton's second law; Newton's third law; Momentum and its conservation
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: D03-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; D04-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; D09-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; D09-1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D01-1#N.6a, D03-1#N.7a, D04-1#N.5, D09-1#N.10a, D01-1#N.12, D03-1#N.2, D04-1#N.4, D09-1#N.16a, D01-1#N.14, D09-1#N.7, D09-1#N.2. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Newton's second law
items.clue: Relationship in which a is proportional to F for one mass and to 1/m for one F.

items.label: Newton's third law
items.clue: Idea that interactions come in pairs of the same type, acting on different bodies.

items.label: Explosion
items.clue: Event in which parts start at rest and move off in opposite directions, total p staying zero.

items.label: Kinetic energy
items.clue: Scalar that increases when a spring pushes two blocks apart from rest, though total p stays zero.

questions.stem: A space probe weighs 4905 N on Earth, where g = 9.81 N kg⁻¹. It lands on Mars, where g = 3.7 N kg⁻¹. What is the probe's mass on Mars?

options.text: 190 kg
500 kg

questions.explanation: m = W/g on Earth = 500 kg. Mass does not depend on location, so it is still 500 kg on Mars (where it weighs 500 × 3.7 = 1850 N).

questions.stem: Block X (2.0 kg) and block Y (4.0 kg) rest on a frictionless horizontal surface, joined by a light string. A horizontal force of 24 N pulls X away from Y, and both accelerate together. What is the tension in the string?
questions.explanation: System: a = 24 ÷ 6.0 = 4.0 m s⁻². Y alone: the only horizontal force is the tension, T = 4.0 × 4.0 = 16 N.

questions.stem: A horse pulls a cart along a level road, and both speed up from rest. A student argues: "The cart pulls back on the horse with a force equal in magnitude to the horse's pull on the cart, so these forces cancel and the cart cannot speed up." Which statement correctly identifies the flaw in the argument?

options.text: The two forces act on different objects, so they cannot cancel.
The horse pulls harder than the cart pulls back while they speed up.
The cart pulls back after the horse's pull has set it moving.
A cart cannot pull on anything, so no force acts back on the horse.

questions.stem: A 0.50 kg trolley moving at 5.0 m s⁻¹ collides with a 3.0 kg trolley at rest on a level track with negligible friction. After the collision, the 0.50 kg trolley moves backwards at 1.0 m s⁻¹ and the 3.0 kg trolley moves forwards at 1.0 m s⁻¹. How much of the system's kinetic energy is transformed into other forms of energy?
A crate is given a push and then slides down a rough ramp on its own. Which list gives all the forces acting on the crate while it slides, and no others?

options.text: Weight, normal force, friction up the ramp and a force of motion down the ramp
Weight, normal force and friction down the ramp
Weight, normal force from the ramp and friction up the ramp
Weight, a separate force down the slope, normal force and friction

questions.explanation: Earth pulls down; the ramp pushes perpendicular to its surface and, as the crate slides down it, rubs back up it. Three forces, each with a source.

questions.stem: A crate slides to the left across a level floor with negligible friction. At one instant, two students push on it horizontally: one pushes to the left with a force of 20 N, and the other pushes to the right with a force of 30 N. Which statement about the crate at this instant is correct?

options.text: Its speed is increasing, as there is a net force exerted on it.
Its acceleration is to the left, the direction it is moving.
Its speed is decreasing, as its acceleration is to the right.
Its speed is constant, as the net force exerted on it is constant.

questions.stem: A lamp hangs at rest from a cord fixed to the ceiling. The cord exerts an upward force on the lamp. Which force forms a Newton's third law pair with this force?

options.text: The gravitational force exerted on the lamp by Earth
The downward force exerted on the cord by the lamp
The upward force exerted on the cord by the ceiling
The gravitational force exerted on Earth by the lamp

questions.explanation: The cord pulls up on the lamp, so the lamp pulls down on the cord: the same contact interaction, equal in size, opposite in direction, on the other object.

questions.stem: A person of mass 60 kg stands in a rowing boat of mass 120 kg. Both are at rest, and water resistance is negligible. The person jumps horizontally from the boat onto a jetty, leaving at 1.0 m s⁻¹. Which statement about the boat immediately afterwards is correct?

options.text: It moves away from the jetty at 1.0 m s⁻¹, as the forces on the person and the boat are equal and opposite.
It stays at rest, as the person pushes off towards the jetty and not against the boat.
It moves away at 0.50 m s⁻¹, with the same kinetic energy as the person.
It moves away at 0.50 m s⁻¹, with momentum equal and opposite to the person's.

questions.stem: A hockey puck is hit by a stick and then slides across level ice. Friction and air resistance are negligible. Which forces are exerted on the puck while it slides, after it has left the stick?

options.text: Earth's pull, the ice's push and a fading push left over from the hit
A downward pull by Earth and an upward push by the ice that touches it
A downward pull by Earth, and no force at all from the ice
An upward push by the ice, with no gravitational force on a supported puck

questions.stem: Two blocks, of masses 1.0 kg and 4.0 kg, are held at rest on a horizontal surface with negligible friction, with a compressed spring between them. When they are released, the 1.0 kg block moves off at 2.0 m s⁻¹. Which statement about the 4.0 kg block is correct?

options.text: It moves off at 2.0 m s⁻¹, in the opposite direction.
It moves off at 0.50 m s⁻¹, in the opposite direction.
It moves off at 8.0 m s⁻¹, in the opposite direction.
It stays at rest, as the total momentum must stay zero.

questions.explanation: Total momentum starts at zero and stays zero: 4.0 × v = 1.0 × 2.0, so v = 0.50 m s⁻¹, opposite to the 1.0 kg block.

questions.stem: A cricket ball of mass m moving horizontally with speed v is struck by a bat. It leaves the bat moving horizontally with speed 3v/2 in the opposite direction. Taking the ball's initial direction of motion as positive, what is the change in the ball's momentum?
